answer: Set a fixed reward ceiling for each task batch, independent of how many keys enter; at close, the contract caps each key at one verified work unit and divides the pool among accepted units, so cloning keys cannot enlarge total payout. A proposed 0.02 POA entry fee, not a live rule, costs 1,000 fake keys 1,000 × 0.02 = 20 POA; one honest key pays 0.02 POA once. An ocean survey might map terrace erosion near the summit. This caps extraction, but many genuinely useful fake-key outputs can still claim much of the fixed pool.
